In the queue outside the chemistry lab, Vaibhav leaned over and grinned. "So, Yamini, is it true your dad moved out and your mum works nights now? Charu said you cry about it in the washroom."
Yamini's stomach dropped like a lift. For a second the corridor went quiet in her ears. She had told exactly one person that, in a whisper, sitting on the terrace steps in August.
She looked down the line. Charu was laughing with the new girls at the front, ponytail swinging, the same Charu who had cried with her that day. Now she looked like someone Yamini had never met.
"Who told you?" Yamini asked, though she knew.
Vaibhav shrugged. "Everyone knows."
When Ms Reddy opened the lab door, Yamini walked in, sat at the back bench and stared at the burner for the whole period, face hot, eyes stinging.

qa.q: Where had Yamini told Charu her secret?
qa.a: Yamini told Charu in a whisper, sitting on the terrace steps in August.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when she looked at Charu in the line?
qa.a: Yamini felt humiliated and heartbroken; Charu, who had once cried with her, now looked like someone she had never met.

qa.q: What could help Yamini in the hours after this shock?
qa.a: Yamini could avoid reacting in the corridor, and later talk to a trusted adult such as Ms Reddy or a parent, so she isn't left holding the shock alone.

qa.q: What would change if Vaibhav had not repeated the rumour?
qa.a: Yamini would have been spared learning it in a crowded queue, and could have faced Charu privately before the story spread further.

grounding: Shows a teenage girl hearing her private family story from a classmate, with humiliation and grief as her trusted friend suddenly seems a stranger.

Manjula,
I'm not going to send this. I just need it out of me.
Today on the school bus, Ritika from 10B turned round and asked if I was "the girl whose brother failed his entrance exam", and whether that's why my parents shout at night. I told only you that. Two weeks ago. You held my hand and said, "I'll never tell anyone, Devu."
My stomach dropped so hard I thought I'd be sick on the bus floor. Everyone near us went quiet, the way people do when they're pretending not to listen.
I've been sitting on my bed for two hours. It isn't only that people know. It's that I keep trying to picture you telling them, and I can't make your face fit. I thought I knew you better than anyone. Tonight I don't know who you are.
Devika

qa.q: What did Manjula say when Devika shared the secret?
qa.a: Manjula held Devika's hand and said, 'I'll never tell anyone, Devu.'

qa.q: What does Devika mean by 'I can't make your face fit'?
qa.a: Devika can't match the friend she trusted with someone who would spread her secret; Manjula suddenly feels like a stranger.

qa.q: Why might writing an unsent letter help Devika right now?
qa.a: It lets Devika get the shock and grief out safely without saying something in anger; later she can decide calmly what to say to Manjula. 🤍

qa.q: What might the people on the bus have felt when Ritika asked the question?
qa.a: They seemed uncomfortable, going quiet and pretending not to listen, which suggests some of them sensed the question was cruel.

grounding: Illustrates a teenage girl hearing her private story from someone else, feeling her stomach drop and seeing her trusted friend as a stranger.

"What? Pradeep, who told you that?"

"Everyone in the bus was talking about it."

"Everyone?"

"Rhea's group. They said Tanisha told them. Sorry, I thought you knew people knew."

"...Tanisha said that?"

"Yeah. Are you okay? You've gone white."

"I told her on Sunday. In her room. She promised."

"Oh. Oh no."

"She promised, Pradeep."

"Do you want to sit down?"

"I don't know. I don't know what I want. I feel like everyone's looking at me."

"No one's looking. Okay, some people are looking. Come, let's go round the back way."

"I thought she was my best friend. I don't even know who that is now."

I found out in the girls' washroom. Two girls from 9C were at the mirrors, and one said, "Did you know Payal's mom and dad sleep in separate rooms? Minakshi told us."

I was in the stall. I didn't move. I stood there with my hand on the latch until they left, because if I came out they'd see my face.

My stomach felt like it had fallen through the floor. I had told Minakshi that on the terrace, at her birthday, when we were the only two people awake. I had cried and she had hugged me.

The worst part wasn't the girls. It was that the Minakshi I knew would never have done that. So either I never knew her, or she changed, and I don't know which is worse.

I skipped lunch and sat in the library pretending to read.

qa.q: Where did Payal hear her secret being repeated?
qa.a: In the girls' washroom, from two girls from 9C.

qa.q: Why does Payal stay in the stall until the girls leave?
qa.a: Payal feels humiliated and shocked and does not want them to see her face.

qa.q: What small step could help Payal after lunch?
qa.a: Payal could talk to a trusted adult or friend about what happened instead of sitting alone, so she is not carrying the shock by herself.

qa.q: What might it be like for the two girls at the mirror if they knew Payal heard?
qa.a: They might feel embarrassed and a little guilty, realising the gossip was a real person's painful secret.

grounding: Payal overhears her private family story in the washroom and feels humiliation and grief, seeing her friend Minakshi as a stranger.

Class teacher's note, Friday

During the break, Avni came into the staffroom corridor and stood near the notice board without speaking. Her face was flushed, and her hands were clenched around her water bottle.

When I asked if she was all right, she said, "Everyone knows about my brother's hospital stay. I only told Seema." Her voice broke on the name.

She said a girl in her class had asked her about it loudly during PE. She looked humiliated and also bewildered: "Seema is my best friend. She wouldn't. But she did."

I took her to the empty resource room and sat with her until the next bell, and let her talk. I told her that her feelings made sense. I informed the school counsellor, who met her after the last period, and I phoned her mother so she would know Avni had a hard day.

— Ms Fernandes

qa.q: Where did the teacher take Avni?
qa.a: To the empty resource room.

qa.q: What was Avni feeling when her voice broke on Seema's name?
qa.a: She felt humiliated and bewildered, grieving that her best friend had told her secret.

qa.q: What did the teacher do well in response?
qa.a: Ms Fernandes noticed Avni's distress, stayed with her, validated her feelings, and passed it on the same day to the counsellor and her mother.

qa.q: How might Seema react when she learns Avni is hurt?
qa.a: Seema may feel guilty and defensive, or ashamed, depending on whether she meant to spread it.

grounding: A teacher's note shows Avni hearing her private family story from someone else, feeling humiliation and grief, and the teacher's same-day support.

passage:
Tuesday

I'm writing this with my door locked.

In the lunch line today, Sanya from 9-C turned round and said, "Hey Tenzin, is it true your dad left because of your mum's shouting?"

My stomach just dropped. Like a lift. I told that to one person. One. Naveen, on the bench behind the gym, in August, when I cried for the first time about it.

I couldn't even answer Sanya. I walked out of the line without my food.

Naveen was at the other table, laughing with his cricket friends. He looked up. He looked away.

I keep thinking about all the times we walked home together. I thought I knew him better than anyone. Now it's like I'm remembering a stranger.

I feel stupid. And sad in a way that's hard to explain, like someone died but nobody did.

qa.q: Who asked Tenzin the question in the lunch line?
qa.a: Sanya from 9-C turned round and said it in the lunch line.

qa.q: What was Tenzin feeling when Sanya repeated the story?
qa.a: Tenzin felt a sudden drop of humiliation and shock, then a heavy grief at losing the friend Tenzin thought Naveen was.

qa.q: What could help Tenzin in the next day or two?
qa.a: Talking to a trusted adult, such as a parent or school counsellor, about both the story spreading and the hurt, rather than carrying it alone.

qa.q: How might Naveen have felt when he looked up and then away?
qa.a: Naveen likely felt ashamed and uncomfortable, knowing he had told the secret.

grounding: A diary shows a teen hearing a private story repeated by someone else, feeling humiliation and grief and seeing a trusted friend as a stranger.
